acceptanceCriteria: Decision recorded (spec tasks-criterion-binding-v0.md) on whether the verdict predicate domain is a distinct closed input from the claim scope, with the rejected alternative
A ticket can declare its full write set as effects.touchPaths and still run cem-verdict touched-anchored over a narrower governed path list
V1-1348's closeout evidence is re-read against the chosen contract and the build-log entry names any re-run needed
body: Friction observed on 2026-10-13 while preparing V1-1348 for criterion 4 of V1-1283. The cem-verdict gate (policy v9, {claim.touchPaths} placeholder, TCB-V0-015) evaluates predicate touched-anchored over the claim-era effects.touchPaths. Only generated spec projection hunks (docs/specs/README.md, REQUIREMENTS.tsv, sometimes INDEX.json) reach tier anchored; ordinary cited hunks are tier cited and fail tier-below-anchored. To make the gate GRANT, V1-1348's effects were declared as exactly docs/specs/README.md and docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv, which is narrower than the paths the lane actually edits, and the real paths then have to be widened after claim (claim with DECLARED effects ignores --scope, see V1-1321). The same field therefore carries two meanings: the Tasks resource reservation (should be the full write set) and the verdict predicate domain (should be the paths whose evidence must be anchored). Expected: a separate, closed predicate input (e.g. a per-gate touchPaths or a ticket requirement-evidence path list) so the claim scope can stay truthful. Actual: one field, two consumers, and the narrower one wins. Related: V1-1356 (candidate must be the seal commit).
title: Ticket effects.touchPaths serves both the claim scope and the cem-verdict predicate, forcing a narrow declaration to make touched-anchored pass
